import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [

        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_53/test_13.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_53/test_14.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file, usecols=['addr_state'])
        # Ensure addr_state is integer type (or convert if possible)
        df['addr_state'] = pd.to_numeric(df['addr_state'], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically (union all rows)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Drop rows where addr_state is null (if any)
    combined_df = combined_df.dropna(subset=['addr_state'])

    # Convert addr_state to plain int (from pandas Int64 nullable)
    combined_df['addr_state'] = combined_df['addr_state'].astype(int)

    # The target schema is just ['addr_state'] integer column
    # The target has 628 tuples, so we keep all rows as is (union all)
    # No aggregation or grouping is explicitly required by the problem statement

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_53/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
